name: Kyagar Glacier Lake (Shaksgam / Yarkant)
historical_glofs: Over 30 recorded historical outbursts (notably 2015, 2016, 2017, and August 2018)
downstream_exposure: Shaksgam valley artery, downstream floodplains, and Yarkant river settlements
sentinel1_coverage: Paths 34 (Desc), 129 (Asc), 136 (Desc). ~14 passes every 2 months. 12-day repeat cycle.
nisar_coverage: Full coverage on planned L-band tracks 69, 120, 170. High penetration through seasonal ice cover.
scientific_references: Round et al. (2017, The Cryosphere); Haemmig et al. (2014, Geomorphology); Bhambri et al. (2019, Remote Sensing)
hackathon_recommendation: TOP RECOMMENDATION (Rank 1): Best global archetype for multi-temporal SAR tracking of ice-dammed surge lakes and annual filling/outburst cycles.

name: Rumbak Glacial Lake
approx_surface_area_ha: Pre-outburst: ~3.0 ha (0.03 km²); Post-outburst: ~0.6 ha residual pond
associated_glacier: Unnamed cirque glacier hanging above Rumbak valley
drainage_basin: Rumbak Nala -> Zingchen Stream -> Indus River (Hemis National Park, Leh)
historical_glofs: 21-22 August 2021 catastrophic moraine breach & debris flow
downstream_exposure: Rumbak village (7 km downstream), Zingchen, trail bridges, and Indus confluence
sentinel1_coverage: Paths 129 (Asc), 136 (Desc). Full Sentinel-1A + 1B constellation coverage directly straddling the August 2021 event.
nisar_coverage: Full coverage on planned L-band tracks. Ideal for breached moraine stability baseline.
scientific_references: NRSC National Hydrology Project Glacial Lake Inventory; Nüsser & Schmidt (2024); SANDRP Investigation (2021)
hackathon_recommendation: TOP RECOMMENDATION (Rank 2): Perfect case study for modern GLOF forensics with dense SAR pre/post coverage and clear breach mechanics.

name: Drang-Drung Proglacial Lake Complex
approx_surface_area_ha: Expanding proglacial lake: ~8.5 ha in 2017 to ~12.3 ha in 2023
associated_glacier: Drang-Drung Glacier (Ladakh's second largest glacier, ~23 km length)
drainage_basin: Stod / Doda River -> Padum -> Zanskar River Basin
historical_glofs: No major historic catastrophic breach; active progressive expansion and potential moraine overtopping hazard
downstream_exposure: Pensi La transport corridor, Stod valley villages, Padum town, Zanskar road infrastructure
sentinel1_coverage: Paths 27 (Asc), 34 (Desc), 136 (Desc). 14 passes per 2 months; dense multi-year time-series (2017, 2020, 2023, 2024).
nisar_coverage: Full L-band coverage. Excellent for distinguishing clean ice, debris mantle, proglacial lake, and moraine rampart.
scientific_references: Mir et al. (2017, Geomorphology); Shukla et al. (2020, Journal of Glaciology); NRSC Indus Atlas (2020)
hackathon_recommendation: TOP RECOMMENDATION (Rank 3): Best site for investigating long-term proglacial lake expansion, glacier terminus calving, and moraine stability.

name: Gya Glacial Lake
approx_surface_area_ha: Pre-outburst: ~14.0 ha; Post-outburst: ~4.5 ha persistent residual water
drainage_basin: Gya Nala -> Miru -> Upshi -> Upper Indus River
historical_glofs: August 2014 catastrophic moraine breach (subglacial piping / tunnel collapse)
downstream_exposure: Gya village (bridges, houses, and farmland destroyed), Leh-Manali Highway (NH-3)
sentinel1_coverage: Paths 129 (Asc), 136 (Desc). Post-event monitoring operational from Oct 2014 onwards.
nisar_coverage: Full L-band coverage. Useful for monitoring residual lake volume and moraine breach channel stability.
scientific_references: Schmidt & Nüsser (2017, Natural Hazards); NRSC Technical Report (2014); HMAGLOFDB (2023)
hackathon_recommendation: STRONG CANDIDATE (Rank 4): Historic moraine breach benchmark; however, Sentinel-1 only became operational in Oct 2014 (post-event only for SAR).

name: Parkachik Glacier Proglacial Lake
approx_surface_area_ha: Formed post-2015 (~1.5 ha); modeled to expand into 3 lakes up to ~50 ha
lake_type: Proglacial lake in overdeepened bedrock trough
drainage_basin: Suru River -> Panikhar -> Sankoo -> Kargil -> Indus Basin
historical_glofs: No historic outburst; high future hazard potential due to rapid snout retreat and subglacial overdeepening
downstream_exposure: Parkachik village, Kargil-Zanskar highway, downstream Suru settlements
nisar_coverage: Full L-band coverage. Ideal for bedrock overdeepening and ice velocity tracking.
scientific_references: Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (WIHG, 2023 Annals of Glaciology); Garg et al. (2022)
hackathon_recommendation: NOTABLE PROSPECT (Rank 5): Emerging proglacial lake with published overdeepening models, but currently smaller water extent than Drang-Drung.

name: Phyang Glacier Watershed Cirque
approx_surface_area_ha: Ephemeral melt ponds < 0.8 ha (no large permanent lake)
lake_type: High-altitude cirque melt ponds & moraine debris slopes
drainage_basin: Phyang Tokpo -> Phyang Village -> Indus River
historical_glofs: July 2006 flood (intense cloudburst/debris flow on glaciated slopes; NOT a classic moraine-dam breach)
downstream_exposure: Phyang monastery, Phyang village, airport perimeter, Leh outskirts
scientific_references: IDSA Report (2006); Wangchuk & SECMOL Ice Stupa Documentation; Nüsser (2019)
hackathon_recommendation: POOR GLOF CANDIDATE (Rank 6): Watershed is dominated by cloudburst-debris flows and downstream artificial ice stupas/reservoirs rather than a major natural GLOF lake.

name: Kyagar Tso (Kiagar Tso), Rupshu
lake_type: Tectonic / Endorheic structural basin lake (NO GLACIAL DAM)
associated_glacier: None in contact (closed endorheic plateau basin)
drainage_basin: Rupshu Changthang closed basin (north of Tso Moriri)
historical_glofs: None (Closed basin, no natural dam, no outflow breach)
scientific_references: GSI Himalayan Geology Studies; Wadia (1931); NRSC Wetland Atlas of Ladakh
hackathon_recommendation: COMPLETELY UNSUITABLE (Rank 7): Natural endorheic saline lake in a structural depression. Has no moraine or ice dam, no glacier contact, and zero GLOF hazard.
